However locals seem to dislike the colony and each evening departure sit banging drum & shacking noisy rattle which disturbs the bat departure causing bats to emerge and scatter rather than forming the dramatic ribbon…

spots.name: Popa Taung Kalat Shrine
spots.desc: To reach the top of the shrine, you must remove shoes and socks and climb the 777 steps to the summit. Take great care during the rainy season as the steps can be very slippery. Along the way are a multitudes of monkeys expecting treats. Sometimes they can get a little aggressive (supposedly, the monkeys like to go after people's glasses) so it is recommended that you keep a tight grip on your…

spots.name: Mount Popa Peak
spots.desc: The hike takes about 1 hr, and on a mist-less day (e.g. during wet season when the air is cleaned by the rain) you can easily spot Bagan. About 1 km before the peak, you will hit a small temple with pagoda. Take enough water and sunscreen for the top.
spots.price: Free, US$10 for a guide (do not trust the price Popa Mountain Resort quotes)

spots.name: Taung Kwe Pagoda
spots.desc: Impressively built on a big rock with many smaller pagodas sticking out. Requires climbing several flights of stairs around the rock to reach the top. At night the temple is lit like a fairground with twinkling lights. Also a good place to weather watch or star gaze on darker platforms. Alternatively, go during dusk or dawn to watch the sunset or sunrise.
spots.price: Free but camera fee of 300/500 kyat (photo) or 1,000 kyat (video)

spots.name: Naung Yar Lake
spots.desc: Tranquil lake in the middle of the city with a wooden bridge crossing it. Popular with local young adults as a hangout spot. Have a picnic here if the mood strikes you.

spots.name: Ngwe Taung Dam
spots.desc: A dam by the town of Demoso, which forms a mirror like lake. A picturesque spot to take pictures with the background fields and hills. The dam regulates the irrigation of surrounding fields

spots.name: Umbrella Pond
spots.desc: Small pond by Demoso with mud that occasionally rise up in several places forming a mound that looks like an umbrella - likely from gas formation within the pond. Said to be lucky if you see one of these umbrellas bubbling up.

spots.name: Htee Sel Khar Waterfalls
spots.desc: Staircase type waterfalls with a pontoon bridge crossing the water straddling Kayah and Shan states. A popular place for a dip with many people from the surrounding area visiting.

spots.name: Seven Lakes
spots.desc: A series of lakes where it was said was formed by 7 mythological creatures who landed in the area. With a backdrop of surrounding hills, it's a scenic location.

spots.name: Kyet Cave
spots.desc: A limestone cave with mysterious ancient wooden coffins inside ranging in sizes. Some coffins are located in hard to reach nooks within the cave. It was said that ancestors of the local population were interred in these coffins inside the cave. There are no visible skeletons or bones. There is a small monastery outside the cave. Within the cave is pitch black without lights (2017), so carry a…

spots.name: Kayan people villages
spots.desc: Ask around which villages are good for visiting or organise a local transport/tour to go around (5,000-10,000 kyat). You will have to decide about the ethics of this form of tourism. Try to find a tour that benefits the local community.

spots.name: Sunboon village
spots.desc: 50 m down, women can be seen sitting weaving with goods for sale. 500 m further on, there are a few wooden houses with Kayan. Older people don't understand Burmese, so an interpreter is suggested if you really want to interact.

spots.name: Naung Yar Market
spots.desc: Local roadside market selling a variety of foods and goods. People travel from the surrounding region to buy and sell here. Go in the morning.

spots.name: Thiri Mingalar Market
spots.desc: Large outdoor market with covered stalls. Many different items sold here including a range of grocery stalls, eateries, souvenir and general goods shops. Pharmacy and electronic stalls are also present.

spots.name: Demoso Market
spots.desc: Large outdoor local market in Demoso. People come here from the surrounding region to buy and sell. Large selection of foods and goods. If you're up for it, try the moonshine from the people selling liquid from what appear to be gas cans. You will see people offering you a liquid in small cups to taste before buying.

spots.name: Mingalar Hin Htote
spots.desc: Popular restaurant known for its Hin Htote (rice flour and meat steamed in a banana leaf), a specialty of the region. Eat it with chili sauce. Busy with both people eating in and buying hin htote for takeout.

spots.name: Shan Noodle Shop
spots.desc: Shop selling Shan noodles, which are rice noodles topped with a mix of spices, peanuts, and chilis. Busy during the breakfast-lunch hours.

spots.name: Shwe Ya Ti
spots.desc: Restaurant with a patio overlooking the Balu Chaung River. Serves traditional Burmese foods such as Burmese curries. Food available pre-made and made to order.

spots.name: Boddhi Tataung
spots.desc: Two big statues of Buddha and a golden pagoda which makes for a pretty amazing sight. One Buddha is standing and the other is lying on its side. You can enter the inside of the standing Buddha which consists of quite a few storeys. The images on the walls mostly depict visions of hell.

spots.name: Thanboddhay Pagoda
spots.desc: Built between 1939 and 1952, the unique feature of this pagoda is its small sculptures of Buddha (said to be more than 500,000). There is a little tower just opposite the pagoda which can be climbed.

spots.name: Golden Arrow Hotel
spots.desc: Rooms look shabby, air-con cannot be adjusted and breakfast consists of cold fried eggs and toast. However the rooms are clean and has a fast Internet connection.
spots.price: Double room with private bathroom and air-con is USD25 (May 2013)

spots.name: Monywa Hotel
spots.desc: Rooms are not new, though fairly clean and equipped with new air-con. Bathrooms are clean. Staff are friendly and helpful. Tuk-tuk ride from bus station to this hotel cost 2,000 kyat.

spots.name: New hotel between the Clock Tower and Bogyoke Statue
spots.desc: New (May 2013), expensive-looking hotel with promotional offers. Extremely friendly staff.

spots.name: Shweyinhmyaw Paya
spots.desc: This pagoda at the north-west end of town has nice views of the sunset. You can watch from a viewing tower or at the side of the river next to the pagoda.

spots.name: Kaw Ka Taung Cave
spots.desc: This is a small and low cave built using tiles and filled with numerous small and big Buddhas. Bring a torch since there is something in the end to explore. Going further just by the cave, after 200 m there is a nice swimming pool with very clear water from the mountain and hundreds of fish in it, circled by half a dozen restaurants right next to beautiful rice fields. Take a swim and get off the…

spots.name: Mat Ka Na Bridge & Village
spots.desc: Sometimes also spelled Lat Ka Na. This concrete bridge is a famous and picturesque destination. Explore the village behind the bridge.

spots.name: Yae Ta Khon
spots.desc: A nice swimming pool in a cool surrounding. Unfortunately, women are not allowed to swim in the upper pool. Following up the hill to the right of the pool there are many white pagodas standing in a geometrical and quite picturesque order.

spots.name: Bayin Nyi Cave
spots.desc: Placed in a beautiful surrounding with a nearby lake and pagoda.

spots.name: Hpa-Pu village and hill
spots.desc: Take a boat across the river to Hpa-Pu and learn something about the history and name of Hpa-an. If you feel energetic you can hike up the hill north of Hpa-Pu.

spots.name: Myo Ma Zay Gyi Market
spots.desc: Everything is sold here from cosmetics to clothing to fruits to gold.

spots.name: Khit Thit
spots.desc: Quite expensive for Myanmar, but a big selection of tasty food and big portions.

spots.name: Lucky Restaurant
spots.desc: Good food, good beer, nicer atmosphere and decoration than Khit Thit.

spots.name: San Ma Tau Restaurant
spots.desc: Great ratings on Google. Lots of side dishes and unlimited veggie food. The fish curry is really good. Serves delicious coconut jaggery with sesame seeds.

spots.name: Shwe Htone Maung Cafe
spots.desc: Praised for its great breakfast including variations of noodles and bananas. Also try the vermicelli.

spots.name: New Day Bakery
spots.desc: Serves fresh (not instant) coffee for a cheap price. They have a great variety of different coffee shakes, iced coffee, frappucino, and fresh fruit juices.
spots.price: From 600 kyat for coffee and fresh juices

spots.name: Mya Kan Thar Food Centre
spots.desc: Provide clean, fresh, healthy and delicious light food. Suitable for who seeking safe food around Hpa-an. The noodle and fried rice dishes are freshly prepared and well cooked and serve while hot. The Shop is located near government offices and quiet place. It is designed with traditional thatch roofing which give nature coolness who getting hot and humid after walking around famous lake "Kan…
spots.addr: Corner of Yone Kone St. and Zwekabin St

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: There is a night market with a huge variety of food, directly at the Kan Thar Yar lake. Just go down the "School Street" from the main road until you see it next to the lake.

spots.name: Veranda Youth Community Cafe
spots.desc: A nice and cool place which is also supporting the local youths development programs. Popular among the local expatriates and there is also a tourists information centre to assist those who might need help to travel around Hpa-An.

spots.name: The Candacraig
spots.desc: Colonial mansion built as a guest house of The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation in 1904. Made famous by Paul Theroux in The Great Railway Bazaar, it is a good place to stop and see how the colonials lived. But, be aware that the house and hotel are now owned by the government. Other colonial houses remade into government run hotels include The Croxton and Craddock Court.

spots.name: Chinese Temple
spots.desc: A large and colourful Chinese temple built by the many Yunanese immigrants to the town.

spots.name: English Cemetery
spots.desc: The cemetery is in very poor condition having been "nationalized" by the junta and most of the headstones are in disrepair with unreadable inscriptions. Still, a few survive and will be worth the time spent if you are a history buff. St James Church, once Anglican but now Catholic, lies across the road. Drop in and see the plaques to the various British lives lost in various wars. The friendly…

spots.name: National Kandawgyi Gardens
spots.desc: Established in 1915 by Alex Rodger as the Maymyo Botanical Gardens, the garden has a rich and diverse collection of flora, including many English plant varieties, and is without a doubt among the most beautiful botanical gardens in the world. A rose garden, a stupa in the middle of a pond and an orchid garden are among the highlights. Seeds are available for sale. A popular spot for locals. Open…

spots.name: Purcell Tower
spots.desc: The clock in this tower is reputed to mime the chimes of Big Ben (or so says Lonely Planet).

spots.name: National Landmarks Garden
spots.desc: A grandiose collection of large models of Burma's landmarks. Generally pretty boring but has interesting touches like proudly displaying oil wells in the middle of a line of stupa. Entrance fee for foreigners is US$4 (or the kyat equivalent).

spots.name: Anisakan Falls
spots.desc: In a rugged gorge and framed at the base by a Buddhist temple, Anisaken Falls makes a good half day hike from Pyin U Lwin. Mandalay-bound pick-ups (300 kyat) drop you at the village of Anisakan (tell the driver you're going to the falls and he'll drop you at the road to the falls rather than in the village itself). From there, follow a long road (about 2 km) through the village, across a railway…

spots.name: Pwe Kauk Falls
spots.desc: Known as Hampshire Falls in British times. Not much to look at by the standards of falls elsewhere, but they are a popular picnic spot and seeing Burmese families picnicking and enjoying themselves is the main reason to go. A precarious bridge crosses the stream and disappears into a fig tree. The falls are on the way to Lashio so you'll need to hire a taxi but, if you want to save money, hang…

spots.name: Pyeik Chin Miang
spots.desc: Further along the road to Lashio are these deep caves full of Buddhas. A large pool a little way down is a popular swimming hole. Share taxis to Pwe Kauk Falls often make the trip.

spots.name: Shan villages
spots.desc: If you're not planning to go on to Hsipaw or Kyaukme, you can stop by at the Shan villages of Mogyopit, Yechando and Ye Negye on your way to Pwe Kauk Falls.

spots.name: Gokteik Viaduct daytrip
spots.desc: You can cross the viaduct and come back the same day. Take the Lashio bound train at 08:22to Naung Paing (700/1,600 kyat ordinary/upper class), the first stop after the viaduct. You will arrive there around 11:50. Get out and take the Mandalay-bound train at 12:30. At around 10:30 the train will stop in Naung Che (Naung Hkio) for about 10 min. This is the stop just before Gokteik and your chance…

spots.name: Aung Padamya Restaurant
spots.desc: This is possibly the best Indian restaurant in all of Myanmar.

spots.name: Krishna Restaurant
spots.desc: An unmarked Indian restaurant serving Indian curries with lentils, chapatis and rice. Well-priced, good home cooked food.

spots.name: South Indian Food Centre
spots.desc: A depressing looking family establishment that nevertheless does amazing thali-style curry meals at low prices. There are numerous small, cheap Indian restaurants around town that also do similar meals.

spots.name: the restaurant with no English name
spots.desc: This restaurant has no English sign or transcripted Burmese name. But it does have an English menu! Go for a traditional set Burmese menu and choose any of their delicious curries. The curry is accompanied by 8 side dishes, 1 massive veggy plate with dressing, a soup, rice and a bowl of more rice to go for seconds or thirds. Plates are refilled by the attentive staff for no extra charge when…

spots.name: Maha Myat Muni Pagoda
spots.desc: This Buddhist temple is distinct from other Burmese temples with its Thai and Chinese influences. The artistic style has parallels to those in Chiang Rung and Chiang Rai.

spots.name: Naung Tung Lake
spots.desc: The principal body of water for the town. You can go and walk around the lake while taking in the stunning views of the hill backdrop behind it. The lake is stagnant but you may feel a nice breeze coming from it.

spots.name: Gard Luang Market
spots.desc: The hill tribes around the valley come down to buy and sell various products. They sometimes dressed in their traditional clothes.

spots.name: Lod Htin Lu
spots.desc: Chinese restaurant with decent noodle options. The multilingual menu in Chinese and English.

spots.name: Cafe 21
spots.desc: Modern cafe restaurant, featuring Western and Asian food, with much variety, such as salads, burgers, pizzas, curry. Wifi available. 3 different rooms including one with air-con. Garden. Staff can speak English.

spots.name: Bamboo Bridge
spots.desc: The bridge has to be rebuilt every year after the rainy season. It is fully built out of bamboo. On the other side of the river is a small town.

spots.name: Kaung Hmu Lon Ancient Historical Pagoda
spots.desc: Quite a pagoda and quite a footbridge across the river at the base of the Himalayan foothills. You may be able to take a boat across the river too.

spots.name: Shwe Myint Wan (the Golden Pagoda)
spots.desc: Very picturesque site with several big Buddha images enshrined on its grounds, one of which is a replica of the golden Buddha image of Mahamuni Temple in Mandalay. Locals claim that this pagoda is more than 1,000 years old.

spots.name: Myikyaungon Temple (the Crocodile Temple)
spots.desc: Very unusual temple on the back of a gigantic crocodile statue. There is also a library on top, but women do not have access. An anti-clockwise series of pictures explains the life of Buddha.

spots.name: Giant Standing Buddha
spots.desc: This complex houses a 20-m-high standing Buddha and a large golden bell shared tower.

spots.name: Pagoda & field of status
spots.desc: Buddha images more than a hundred similar sitting behind this sight.

spots.name: Hill pagoda
spots.desc: This temple is on a hill that is a 200-m-walk from the previous one. It also has a big pagoda and gives a good view of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Market
spots.desc: Explore this single street market of 2 km length and its side roads for an authentic Myanmar.

spots.name: Shwe Saryan Pagoda
spots.desc: Believed to have been first built in the 5th century BC, it is the most famous pagoda in the town. The pagoda has a golden colour and a bell-like shape.

spots.name: Shwe Sandaw Pagoda
spots.desc: This pagoda offers the perfect view to take pictures of the giant, sitting Buddha (Sehtatgyi).
spots.price: 3,000 kyat (take the stairs to avoid it)

spots.name: Pagoda
spots.desc: This pagoda offers a great view of Pyay and the surrounding area.

spots.name: Tharaykhittaya Archaeological Museum
spots.desc: An interesting collection of artifacts found around the ruins, showing bronze, ceramic and stone funerary urns, silver coins and bowls, jewellery, carved stone Buddhist and Hindu figures as well as ceramic votive plaques.

spots.name: Shwe Myethman Pagoda
spots.desc: A Buddha with glasses, and the 80 Buddhas Monastery. There are other pagodas within 400 m diameter around Shwe Myethman. Also see this , 2 km before Shwe Myethman.

spots.name: Shwe Bontha Muni Pagoda
spots.desc: The Shwe Bontha Muni Buddha is supposed to be one of three replicas of the Maha Myat Muni Buddha, believed to date to 554 BCE when Sandar Thuriya, the king, ruled.

spots.name: Sri Ksetra
spots.desc: Even if you have seen Bagan, this sight is well-worth the visit. In 2014, Sri Kshetra, Halin and Beikthano (the Pyu cities) have been declared UNESCO World Heritage.

spots.name: Akauk Taung
spots.desc: In the cliff carved, beautiful Buddha statues. Best be seen by boat from the river. In addition, you can make a stop and explore the temples and Buddhas on top of Akuak Tuang mountain, which takes about one hour.

spots.name: Pyay Say Gyi Market
spots.desc: Try this market for the typical items found on Burmese markets.

spots.name: May Ywet War Myanmar Restaurant
spots.desc: A wide range of delicious curries. Top choice among all restaurants in Pyay.

spots.name: Grandma's Restaurant
spots.desc: Good western and South Korean food by the owner Banyar Aung, who has worked as a cook in Kuala Lumpur.

spots.name: Eat Hotpot BBQ and Cafe
spots.desc: Serve yourself all you can eat hotpot and BBQ for 6,000 kyat.

spots.name: Thandaung Gyi
spots.desc: Old colonial hill station which is home to Naw Bu Baw prayer mountain and some other sights. There have been reports that the area is closed, however it was opened in June 2013; a passport check is usually not required before entering the area, but make sure to bring copies anyway. There are multiple B&Bs in the village (8,000-30,000 kyat). There are several routes up and down, the cheapest…

spots.name: Naw Bu Baw
spots.desc: The name of a mountain, and the lady who is said to guard it. The mountain is highly regarded by Karen Christians, and is accessed through the old British hill station town of Thandaung Gyi (pronounced "than down gee") (NB this is not the same town as the newer relocated Than Daung at the bottom of the mountain).

spots.name: Shitthaung Pagoda
spots.desc: This pagoda is still being used by local people. Many angled corridors can be found inside, along which interesting stone carving work can be admired and photographed, like the 550 Jakata (birth name of Buddha) reliefs. The name means 80,000 Buddhas, and so more than 80,000 (actually 84,000) displays of Buddha can be found here. The other name of the pagoda, Ran Aung Zeya, means "victory over the…
spots.price: Use the northern entrance and turn right immediately if you want to avoid the fee. However, walking towards the Buddha…

spots.name: Htukkam Thein Temple
spots.desc: This temple was built in 1571 by king Minphalaung on sand stone. The entrance is to the east and the temple is famous for its internal stone sculptures. It inhabits many displays of live at the royal court. In addition, 140 Buddha statues are lines along the interestingly circling corridors.

spots.name: Mya Tan Zaung (west)
spots.desc: Erected by king Minsawmon in 1430 and part of a sibling pagoda right next to it.

spots.name: Pitaka Taik
spots.desc: Great for sunset due to its location uphill, to whose feet Shitthaung and Htukkam Thein can be found.

spots.name: Sakya Man Aung
spots.desc: This is an attractive pagoda. Dating to 1629, this pagoda was built by king Thirithudhammaraza. At a height of 33 m, this sight displays the ground layout of a lotus blossom.
spots.price: City pass might be checked here

spots.name: Koe Thaung Temple
spots.desc: This used to be the biggest pagoda in Mrauk U but has fallen apart during the past centuries.

spots.name: Archaeological Museum
spots.desc: A collection of artifacts from the Mrauk U sites: Buddhas, slabs with inscriptions, Wethali era coins, paintings that show Mrauk U in its heyday, and an excellent model of Mrauk U that will help you get your bearings. Crumbling walls are all that remains of the royal palace itself.

spots.name: Letse Kan Gate & Let Se Lake (sunset)
spots.desc: Also a great (aim for the GPS marker) and allows for a stroll through the less touristic areas of the city. Great pictures of the nearby pagoda can be taken at dusk from the western side of the opposite sports ground.

spots.name: Sunrise Hill
spots.desc: Walk into the monastery and from there up the hill. This set of pagodas allow for a great view of Mrauk U and the surrounding area. Depending on the time of year, it could be that a lot of mist blocks your view.

spots.name: Wethali
spots.desc: Now a small village but fifteen hundred years ago Wethali was the capital of an ancient Arakan kingdom. While temples are probably buried under the many mounds that dot the area, the only thing to see today is the layout of the palace and a statue known as the Great Image of Hsu Taung Pre.

spots.name: Mahamuni Pagoda
spots.desc: Once housed the Mahamuni Buddha that now resides in the Mahamuni Pagoda in Mandalay. There are several ancient artifacts on view here and at the small museum nearby. Hire a jeep ($30-50) for a day for Wethali and the Mahamuni Pagoda, or take a local pickup or shared taxi up north.
spots.price: 7,500 kyat per person for a tour Wethali and the Mahamuni Pagoda booked in town or at your guesthouse

spots.name: Launggret and Parein
spots.desc: The trip there is done by boat and takes 30 minutes. The only things left to see are Taungmawtaung hill and the Kadothein shrine (15 km south). Further sights around Mrauk U like this are Pataw and Vesali.
spots.price: Take a local pickup or bus

spots.name: Kyauktaw, Dhanywaddy & Salagiri Hill
spots.desc: Salagiri Hill offers spectacular views of the river, nearby bridge and surrounding area.

spots.name: Hari Taung
spots.desc: Climb this hill for a great view of the underlying royal palace and the city.

spots.name: Chin Villages
spots.desc: Day trips to semi-remote villages of the Chin people can be arranged at most hotels. The trip there takes about 3 h one-way, includes lunch and 2-3 villages. Tickets are most probably sold by your hotel or guesthouse, but they will inherit a steep extra fee. Better try the agents or cheaper guesthouses in the city centre and compare prices.

spots.name: Mo Cherry Restaurant
spots.desc: Offers good Chinese and semi-authentic Rakhine food. The food is good and less risky than the places in the market but, if you have the time explore other restaurants, often unnamed, and you'll be pleasantly surprised.

spots.name: Pyae Wa Restaurant
spots.desc: Authentic Rakhine food. The cashew chicken and butterfish is good.

spots.name: Nan Daw Pagoda (Thandwe)
spots.desc: This pagoda on top of a hill 50-60 m above the surrounding area offers a great view of Thandwe and the river. Recommended for sunrise, but you have to get up early.

spots.name: "Dead" Monk
spots.desc: This monastery houses a monk who is said to be in a state of death through meditation for since the 1980s. The "mummy" is kept under glass and cannot be touched. A second monk has "joined".

spots.name: Shiva Temple
spots.desc: Hindu temple to the god Shiva.

spots.name: Wat Jom Kai
spots.desc: A golden pagoda built in the 13th century by the Shan.

spots.name: Star Rain Pub
spots.desc: Gets lively Thai crowds.

spots.name: Myawaddy Complex
spots.desc: Casino and duty-free shops.

spots.name: Sehtatgyi
spots.desc: Giant, sitting Buddha.

spots.name: San Francisco Restaurant
spots.desc: Not very good value for money.

spots.name: Hline Ayar Restaurant
spots.desc: Great for sunset, including extensive English menu.

spots.name: Jade Dragon
spots.desc: Coffee, tea and little snacks.

spots.name: Romeo Cold Cafe
spots.desc: Another riverside option good for a chill and tea.

spots.name: KBZ Bank
spots.desc: ATM and money exchange

spots.name: Shwe Moe Restaurant
spots.desc: Local rice and curry are available
spots.addr: near the Mrauk U post office on the main road

spots.name: For You
spots.desc: Highly recommended, offers a wide range of dishes.

spots.name: Thandwe Government Market
spots.desc: Local products ranging from food to clothing.

spots.name: Rainbow Bakery & Cafe
spots.addr: 87, U Kyaw Yin Street, 3 Quater, Thandwe, Rakhine State, Myanmar 07171

spots.name: The Death Railway Museum
spots.desc: Opened in 2016. Gives an insight to the history of the Burma-Siam railway.

spots.name: Lake in the town centre
spots.desc: Because of the Ye Lann Payer pagoda, right in the middle of the lake, fishing is not allowed, but you can buy some rice crisps at the entry of the bridge to the pagoda, to feed the fish.

spots.name: Bawgyo Paya
spots.desc: A revered Shan pagoda. In addition to the usual complement of Buddhas, the pagoda also has some ancient statues of Hindu origin in the plaza outside.

spots.name: Central Market
spots.desc: One of the best markets to visit in all of Myanmar. Shans, Kachins and other tribals come here to trade regularly. Because so few tourists visit Hsipaw, the merchandise is primarily for villagers who go there to shop. Radios, spare parts, diverse foodstuffs and Shan clothing (trousers, hats, sandals) and the ubiquitous lyongi. The market begins and ends early, starting at 03:30 and is largely…

spots.name: Shan Palace
spots.desc: The Sawbwas of Hsipaw lived here. The last Sawbwa disappeared during the military coup in 1962 and the palace is cared for by his nephew and his nephew's wife. It was possible to visit parts of the palace but this is no longer possible since the nephew, Mr Donald (Sao Oo Kya), is in prison apparently for saying bad things about the military.

spots.name: Nam Tuk Waterfall
spots.local: ၼမ်ႉတူၵ်းတၢတ်ႇ ၼမ်ႉတုၵ်း
spots.desc: A nice water fall. Possibility to swim. It takes around 2 hr to walk from Hsipaw. Less if you take the bike to the start of the real path (near a monastery). On the path it's not possible to ride a bicycle. Very off the beaten path and relaxing. Less water during summer.

spots.name: Mr Shake/Yuan Yuan
spots.desc: Offers freshly mixed juice according to the guests wish i.e. just name some fruits and he will mix it, including alcoholic ingredients. Guests may write down their very own recipe onto a board. The shake seemed to be safe. It has some food as well.

spots.name: Mr Food
spots.desc: Along with the usual Chinese and Shan fare, draught beer (700 kyat) is available.

spots.name: Unnamed Shack
spots.desc: Serves Burmese food. No menu or sign but you'll recognise it by the big pots full of curries outside. The food is good but, since it is prepared in the morning, best to go for lunch.

spots.name: The Club Terrace
spots.desc: The newer and fancier place on the riverfront, it has a stunning location and reasonable food.

spots.name: A Kaung Kyite
spots.desc: Cheap local Burmese food. Many side dishes with rice and refills.

spots.name: Thein Taung Monastery
spots.desc: The monastery is situated on a hill and offers a nice view of the town.

spots.name: Thirigayha Restaurant
spots.local: သီရိဂေဟာ ညီအစ်မ ၇ ဖော်
spots.desc: Tasty Burmese fare made with fresh produce in this cozy cottage. Get the fragrant coconut rice to go with your curries.

spots.name: Pyae Pyae - Shan Noodle Food & Clay Pot Noodle Soup
spots.local: ပြည့်ပြည့်
spots.desc: Great local restaurant. Go for the clay hot pot (2,500 kyat) that is served still sizzling, with omelette, quail's egg, chicken, carrots and greens and might fill two. Do not miss the tea leaf salad (500 kyat) with crunchy peanuts. It might be the only one in Myanmar that is not spicy.

spots.name: Pine Land Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves a variety of Chinese food and wines. Free Wi-Fi for customers.

spots.name: Hi bar
spots.desc: around the central pagoda: wonderful place to spend an evening. Locals are very eager to play the guitar, they even know quite some English songs. Good Rum Sour and Whisky Sour. They also have a donation box for the local hospital.

spots.name: Market
spots.desc: The local market, populated by vendors from villages near and far, is worth a visit. The market closes in mid-morning. A second market caters to day tourists from Thailand.

spots.name: Shwedagon Paya
spots.desc: The main pagoda in town, it is large and gilded. Not to be confused with its namesake in Yangon.

spots.name: Regina Casino
spots.desc: Try your luck here, a short 100-baht tuk-tuk ride from the border. They're the same people who own the golf course. Definitely for low rollers, you can play roulette with 10-baht chips. They've also got blackjack, craps and gaming machines. If you change 2,000 baht into chips you get a free Thai lunch. You can change remaining chips afterwards. A casino minibus will take you back to the border.

spots.name: The Circle Cafe
spots.desc: A modern, air-conditioned cafe and restaurant. The second floor has scenic mountains views.

spots.name: Kyaiktiyo village(s)
spots.desc: The village(s) behind the Golden Rock are interesting and allow for some steep walks up and down along the ridge. You can buy little things, have a coffee, a sweet coconut drink or a Burmese meal, and look at the dead animal shrines put up in the stalls every 50 m or so. Since this is on the opposite side of the pagoda area, don't leave your shoes in the lockers at the beginning if you want to do…

spots.name: Beer River
spots.desc: Beer River is a small swimming area with several restaurants and bars. You can sit on some tables that are in knee-deep water, others that are in the shade. The water is relatively clean and it is a great place to cool off on hot days.

spots.name: Suwannagiri Monastery
spots.desc: Buddhist temple built by the Mon Buddhist monk Luangpho Uttama. Most famous for its hundred wooden pillars and interior walls decorated with beautiful Burmese art.

spots.name: Taung Waing Monastery
spots.desc: Buddhist monastery which as a large Buddha statue in the middle setting a cross-legged, meditative position.

spots.name: Shwe San Daw Pagoda
spots.desc: This temple dominates Ye's town centre. From here you have a nice view of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Banana Mountain Monastery
spots.desc: Famous monastery. Domestic tourists come from far and wide to visit this elaborate hilltop temple and monastery. Great view.

spots.name: Boat ride up the Ye river
spots.desc: First take a motorbike to Kyaung Ywar. From there it is possible to rent a boat and cruise upstream to the Kyaung Nga Kwa pagoda. Scenic views along the way are guaranteed.

spots.name: View from Shwe Maw Daw pagoda
spots.desc: Before going back to Ye go up to this pagoda perched on a hilltop. Enjoy splendid views down to Ye river, which makes a U-turn at this location.

spots.name: Bin Le Wa Beach
spots.desc: Wide beach next to the village Bin Le Wa. Have a stopover in Asin and/or Duya on your way there.

spots.name: Ka Byar Wa Beach
spots.desc: Much nicer beach than Bin Le War but further away (around 1h by motorbike).

spots.name: Lover's Island
spots.desc: Walk across a sandbar at low tide to reach Lover's Island. This island is small and consists of a concrete statue of a Mermaid, a small religious site at the base of the island, and steps leading up to a small circuit of trails. Bring shoes due to the rocky underground. If you can get snorkeling gear, you can try it here instead of hiring a boat to Bird Island.

spots.name: Beach Pagodas
spots.desc: In Myanmar pagodas can be found in even the remotes places, since every person with a little bit of money wants to erect and distributes its own one. Hence, find another two on top of two rocks right here at the beach.

spots.name: Bird Island
spots.desc: This island is located hours from shore and is nothing more than a rocky outcropping in the sea used by local fishermen to dry fish. The rocks are extremely sharp and there is not much to see. Reputed to be the worst island in Myanmar. However, since there is not much to do in Ngwe Saung, it is popular for excursions and bird watching. You can also organise a snorkeling, e.g. trip with "Mr Win"…

spots.name: Elephant camp
spots.desc: This is also a school for children, and has 32 pupils aged between 5 & 14 years. Get your ticket at the just after All Seasons Hotel on the other side of the road.

spots.name: Jasmine Restaurant
spots.desc: They have BBQ seafood and meat including delicious side dishes. Good value for money.

spots.name: Soe KoKo Beach House & Restaurant
spots.desc: The restaurant serves a delicious variety of Myanmar, Thai and Chinese dishes as well as fresh seafood in a relaxing atmosphere, indoors and open air. Breakfast, lunch and dinner. Tea, coffee, beer.

spots.name: Silver Blue Sea
spots.desc: This is a very pleasant and well located restaurant with a vast menu including vegetarian options.

spots.name: UME Japanese Restaurant & Café
spots.desc: Nightly fire shows. Japanese and western menu. Beer and Music.

spots.name: Kyauktan Ye Le Pagoda
spots.desc: The pagoda is on an island in the middle of the river. It was built by King Zeyasana, the seventh king of the Pada Dynasty in the third century BCE. The first pagoda was only 3 m high. The only way to get into the pagoda is by the boat. Foreigners are required to sit in a larger boat which differs from the smaller ones that the locals take due to security purposes. A hefty price of 5,000 kyat is…

spots.name: Pearl Island
spots.desc: Most hotels organise snorkeling trips to the island. But you can also ask restaurants and other shops, which will probably give you a decent bargain. Trips can include snorkeling and fishing. There is even a restaurant on the island, Lobster Bar, the only one, which serves drinks and food.
spots.price: About 15,000 kyat to rent a boat

spots.name: Black Sand Island
spots.desc: Another interesting place to enjoy a picnic and the sunset, or take photos of the picturesque surroundings. This island climbs up to about 40 m and can be reached by bicycle.

spots.name: Amata Mountain
spots.desc: Start early to Jate Taw/Gyeiktaw Village in the south. In the morning you can watch the local fishermen unload their catch from the night before. Afterwards, from the village walk up the mountain. There you will find a standing Buddha (21 m) and a meditation centre to relax and spend some time. Afterwards go on to Abe Village, famous for the mangrove forest and authentic people.

spots.name: Andrew Bay
spots.desc: Rent a bicycle and explore the area by yourself, especially Andrew Bay in the south. Have a tea and watch the busy locals. Ask a local fishermen to take you for a tour onto and even across the bay. The way back, in case you decide not to take the boat, along the road north passing by Thandwe is 41 km, so either have a good bicycle or take a local pickup.

spots.name: Ngapali Golf Course
spots.desc: Can be under water. Go early to avoid the heat and spend 2 hr or so. The old building is the so-called clubhouse. No golf shoes required.

spots.name: Kayaking
spots.desc: Ideal to explore the numerous bays and mangrove forests around Ngapali. Ask at your hotel or the village for renting the kayak, or try Bayview Beach Resort or Art of Sand Beach Bar.

spots.name: Ballooning
spots.desc: Explore the area around Ngapali and Thandwe. Could make more sense to save the ballooning money for Bagan if you go there.
spots.price: US$200-400, depending on the number of people

spots.name: Massage
spots.desc: There are several massage options both attached to the resort and informal tables on the beach.
spots.price: 12,000 kyat for 60 min at Head to Toe resort massage.

spots.name: Trekking
spots.desc: From Ngapali to the countryside, jungle and mountain with incredible views, local knowledge and lunch. Ask around for the best deals.

spots.name: Min Thu Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Seafood is the point about this restaurant. If you definitely aim for fresh fish, go here. Family run and around for a while now.

spots.name: Sea Queen
spots.desc: In case Min Thu is too far away, try this highly recommended restaurant. You will choose your fresh fish outside, which is then prepared in the kitchen inside.

spots.name: Green Umbrella
spots.desc: Lovely restaurant right next to the street. Some people complain about the drinks, so probably go for a beer. Otherwise, delicious seafood and Burmese food, as well as friendly staff.

spots.name: Sunset Bar
spots.desc: Seafood, Burmese, Thai and western food. Highly recommended. Good for a relaxing drink in the evening, but you can also enjoy the food.

spots.name: Five Buddha Hill or Nine Buddha Hill
spots.desc: Sunset watching.

spots.name: Win Moe Tea House
spots.desc: Serves authentic Thai food.

spots.name: Thar Lay Mon Food
spots.desc: The best place to try Mon traditional food.

spots.name: Morning Market
spots.desc: Lots of fish, vegetables and other goods are sold here.

spots.name: Gold Market
spots.desc: Buy all types of jewelry here.

spots.name: Golden Myanmar Restaurant
spots.desc: Seafood shack with local specialties.

spots.name: Royal Flower Restaurant
spots.desc: Live music & cocktails.

spots.name: Two Brothers Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves delicious barracuda, snapper and white tuna.

spots.name: Ngapali Kitchen
spots.desc: Locally run and authentic.

spots.name: Thiripyitsayn Food & Drink
spots.desc: They have good Shan noodles for 500 kyat, and also a very good avocado juice for 500 kyat.

spots.name: Pokala Island
spots.desc: Pokala Island is particularly beautiful, and just a short motorcycle-boat trip away from the main beach street. This also requires a short boat ride (1,000 kyat return). Inhabitants of the island are local fishermen, living together with their families in the houses on the island. A walk around the island reveals remote beaches as well as sharp & rocky coastline.

spots.name: White sand beaches
spots.desc: Some say they are cleaner. Walking there, go past the small pagoda standing on a small hill in the water, there is another pagoda further up, with three large rocks in the water. You can get there by motorcycle, but the road is muddy with many ruts. Even though you might want to consider Ngwe Saung to be the next stop instead of a day trip.
